title: Cross-domain Rumor Detection via Test-Time Adaptation and Large Language Models

live_model.evidence: Gpt-4o-2024-05-13 is adopted to generate pseudo-labels (Section 4.1); Table 1 row 'GPT-4o 0.643 0.629 0.598 0.681 ...' as an LLM baseline

prompt.location: Appendix B / Table 7 (base, conf and conf_reason prompts used in T2ARD)
prompt.note: Which of the Table 7 prompts produced the Table 1 GPT-4o baseline is not stated explicitly (presumably 'base').

claim.location: Table 1, row GPT-4o, block 'Source TWITTER / Target Twitter-COVID19', column Acc.; 400 events (Table 6)

data.source: Twitter-COVID19 and Weibo-COVID19 (Lin et al. 2022) plus TWITTER/WEIBO datasets; public via prior work (post availability may vary)

notes: GPT-4o also serves as the pseudo-label annotator inside T2ARD (role A). Decoding parameters not stated.

resolution.plan: Use the Table 7 'base' prompt (Role / Event: <Event content> / Task with <list of categories> rumor vs non-rumor, python-dict answer) with the 400 Twitter-COVID19 events of Lin et al. 2022 (public release; Table 6); query gpt-4o-2024-05-13 once per event, parse the dict answer and compute accuracy vs 0.643 (Table 1).
resolution.approximation: The paper does not say which Table 7 variant produced the Table 1 GPT-4o baseline (base assumed; conf/conf_reason yield the same label field); what <Event content> holds (source post only vs thread) and decoding parameters are unstated; tweet availability may have decayed.
